title: ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON INQUIRY INTO HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSES SUFFERED BY PERSONS AFFECTED BY HANSEN'S DISEASE AND ON PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO SUCH VICTIMS

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON INQUIRY INTO HUMAN RIGHTS ABUSES SUFFERED BY PERSONS AFFECTED BY HANSEN'S DISEASE AND ON PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO SUCH VICTIMS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Inquiry into Human Rights Abuses Suffered by Persons Affected by Hansen's Disease and on Providing Assistance to Such Victims and its Enforcement Decree, and matters necessary for their implementation. <Amended March 29, 2016>

Article 2 (Composition of the Working Committee)
(1) The relevant public officials who serve as members of the Working Committee for Inquiry into Human Rights Abuses Suffered by Persons Affected by Hansen's Disease (hereinafter the "Working Committee") under Article 4(3) of the Act on Inquiry into Human Rights Abuses Suffered by Persons Affected by Hansen's Disease and on Providing Assistance to Such Victims (hereinafter the "Act") shall be persons designated by the heads of their respective agencies from among Grade III or IV public officials of the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the Ministry of Planning and Budget, the National Police Agency, the National Human Rights Commission, and Jeollanam-do. <Amended March 19, 2010; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; March 29, 2016; August 4, 2017; July 16, 2019; December 30, 2025>
(2) A member who is not a public official shall serve a two-year term and may be reappointed only once. However, the term of a member newly commissioned due to the dismissal or other departure of a member who is not a public official shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term. <Amended March 29, 2016; July 16, 2019>
(3) The Minister of Health and Welfare may remove or dismiss a member of the Working Committee who falls under any of the following: <Inserted March 29, 2016>
1. The member becomes unable to perform duties due to a physical or mental disability;
2. The member commits misconduct in connection with duties;
3. The member is deemed unsuitable to serve due to neglect of duties, impairment of dignity, or other reasons;
4. The member expresses that it is difficult to continue performing duties.

Article 3 (Duties of the Chairperson)
(1) The chairperson of the Working Committee shall represent it and exercise overall control of its work.
(2) If the chairperson cannot perform duties for unavoidable reasons, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf.

Article 4 (Meetings of the Working Committee)
(1) The chairperson shall convene and preside over meetings of the Working Committee.
(2) A meeting shall open with a majority of the members in office present, and a resolution shall require the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.

Article 5 (Allowances)
(1) Allowances may be paid within budgetary limits to members attending the Working Committee. This shall not apply to a member who is a public official attending in direct connection with that member's assigned duties.
(2) Travel expenses and actual expenses may be paid within budgetary limits to witnesses or persons providing information who attend meetings of the Working Committee.
(3) Other details necessary for the operation of the Working Committee shall be determined by the chairperson following deliberation by the Working Committee.

Article 6 (Reports by Victims and Bereaved Families)
(1) To enable victims and bereaved families to report harm under Article 4(2)1 of the Act, the chairperson of the Working Committee shall announce the reporting period, procedures, and other relevant matters through at least two daily newspapers (meaning those registered for nationwide distribution under Article 9(1) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, Etc.), an internet website, or other effective means. <Amended March 29, 2016; January 7, 2021>
(2) A person intending to report as a victim or bereaved family member under paragraph (1) shall submit the victim report in attached Form 1 to the chairperson of the Working Committee with the following documents, including electronic documents:
1. One copy of the basic certificate under the Act on Registration of Family Relations (a family relations certificate for a bereaved family member), or, for a deceased or missing person whose status cannot be verified through the family relations register, one certified copy of the victim's removed family register. Where no removed family register exists, a statement of reasons in attached Form 2 shall be submitted;
2. Where residual disability results from an incident specified in any item of Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act, one medical certificate issued by a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a medical school, or a hospital designated by the Working Committee;
3. Other evidence substantiating the harm. Where it is difficult to attach such evidence, one guarantee confirming the facts of harm in attached Form 3.
(3) Among persons intending to report under paragraph (2), those residing abroad may report to an overseas diplomatic mission. The head of the mission shall submit reports received there to the chairperson of the Working Committee.
(4) The chairperson receiving reports under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall enter them in the victim report receipt register in attached Form 4 and manage and retain the register.
(5) Other details concerning reports of harm by victims and bereaved families shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Working Committee.

Article 7 (Investigation of Harm)
(1) Before requesting a review by the Commission for Inquiry into Human Rights Abuses Suffered by Persons Affected by Hansen's Disease under Article 3 of the Act (hereinafter the "Full Commission"), the chairperson of the Working Committee receiving a report under Article 6 shall verify or investigate the information in the victim report and supporting documents.
(2) Where necessary for verification or investigation under paragraph (1), the chairperson may request relevant agencies, heads of overseas diplomatic missions, or relevant persons to submit materials, provide other necessary information, or state their opinions. Those receiving the request shall actively cooperate.
(3) Necessary matters concerning the methods and items of verification and investigation under paragraph (1) shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Working Committee.

Article 8 (Review and Determination of Victims)
(1) After verification or investigation under Article 7(1) and (2), the chairperson of the Working Committee shall prepare an investigation report and request a review by the Full Commission.
(2) The Full Commission receiving the request under paragraph (1) shall determine victim status within 90 days of receipt and notify the Working Committee of the result.
(3) Upon receiving notification under paragraph (2), the chairperson of the Working Committee shall send the reporter a notice of determination of victim status in an incident involving persons affected by Hansen's disease in attached Form 5, and prepare and maintain the list of victims of such incidents in attached Form 6.

Article 9 (Facility Standards and Eligibility for Admission to Residential Welfare Facilities for Persons Affected by Hansen's Disease)
(1) The facility standards for residential welfare facilities and medical welfare facilities for persons affected by Hansen's disease under Article 10(2) of the Act shall be governed, respectively, by the standards for residential welfare facilities and medical welfare facilities for older persons under Articles 33(3) and 35(3) of the Welfare of Older Persons Act, applied mutatis mutandis.
(2) Persons eligible for admission to the facilities under paragraph (1) shall be those determined to be victims under Article 8 who wish to be admitted.
(3) Other details concerning the establishment and operation of these residential welfare and medical welfare facilities shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare. <Amended March 19, 2010>
